stepsTitle: How it works: convert JSON to CSV

steps.title: Open or paste your JSON
steps.text: Drop a .json file, choose it, or press Ctrl+V to paste JSON. It should be an array of objects, or a single object.

steps.title: It opens as a table
steps.text: Each object becomes a row in the CSV viewer. Nested objects are flattened with dots (address.city) and lists with their position (items.0.name).

steps.title: Filter and edit it
steps.text: Search, sort, filter and edit the rows in the CSV viewer before you save.

steps.title: Download
steps.text: Download saves a .csv file with the JSON file's name. For a semicolon, tab or pipe, choose Download options in the More menu.

handlesTitle: What the JSON to CSV converter handles
handles: Input: a JSON array of objects, or one object, from a .json file or pasted text, up to 10 MB.
Nested data: objects flattened into dot-notation columns such as address.city; lists into items.0, items.1.
Columns: every key that appears in any object, in the order they first appear; missing values are left empty.
Long numbers: integers beyond 2^53 are written digit for digit, not rounded.
Delimiters: a comma, with the byte order mark Excel needs when there is non-Latin text; a semicolon, tab or pipe from Download options.
limits: The JSON must be a list of records (or hold one); other shapes can't become a table.
faqTitle: JSON to CSV: questions and answers

faq.question: How are nested objects turned into columns?
faq.answer: Each nested key is joined to its parent with a dot. {"address": {"city": "Riyadh"}} becomes a column named address.city holding Riyadh.

faq.question: What happens to arrays inside the objects?
faq.answer: Each item gets its position in the column name: tags.0, tags.1, or items.0.name for a list of objects. An empty list is written as [].

faq.question: What JSON shapes can be converted?
faq.answer: An array of objects, which gives one row per object, or a single object, which gives one row. A list of plain values or a number on its own is not a table, so the page says so.

faq.question: My objects do not all have the same keys. Is that a problem?
faq.answer: No. The CSV gets a column for every key found in any object, and a row leaves the cell empty where its object has no such key.

faq.question: My JSON has an error. Can I still convert it?
faq.answer: Not until it is valid. The page shows what is wrong; the JSON validator shows the line and column and repairs common mistakes.

faq.question: Is my JSON uploaded?
faq.answer: No. The JSON is parsed and converted by your browser on your device; nothing is sent to a server.
